children: British government bonds staged a partial recovery on Friday after a heavy selloff a day earlier, helped by easing oil prices following a report that foreign ministers in the Middle East are trying to work out a temporary deal with Iran.

Short-dated gilt yields, sensitive to interest rate expectations, retraced around half of Thursday's move, one of the sharpest in months. The 2-year gilt yield (GB2YT=RR), which moves inversely to the price, was down 7 basis points on the day at 4.81% at 1000 GMT, having leapt 16 bps on Thursday.

Gilts mostly outperformed other major bond markets on Friday, reflecting their sensitivity to energy market moves given Britain's reliance on imported energy and the bearing it has on the inflation outlook.

Longer-dated gilt yields fell by around 3-4 bps on the day, with little immediate reaction to better-than-expected economic growth data for July, after 10-year yields (GB10YT=RR) hit a 19-year high of 5.38% on Thursday and 20- and 30-year yields rose to the highest since 1998.

While a stronger economy usually lifts expectations for higher interest rates, it is also positive for Britain's strained public finances, lifting the gross domestic product denominator that its fiscal rules are measured against.
Investors on Friday priced in a 90% chance of a quarter-point increase in Bank of England interest rates by November, which had been fully priced in on Thursday.
The curve shows a further three interest rate hikes taking place during 2027.
